known_facts: At 10:04 UTC, the checkout error-rate alert fired with an increase from 0.4% to 9%
Deployment dep-1842 for checkout-api completed at 10:01 UTC
Database latency increased around the same time
The external payment provider reported intermittent errors
assumptions: There was a configuration or environment change during deployment dep-1842
Checkout API is dependent on the database and the payment provider
Intensive checks for service credentials were performed before and after the deployment
missing_information: Database query logs that indicate changes in SQL queries or execution plans
Dependency health metrics from other services that might have been affected
Service credential checks before and during the deployment, including expiration dates

candidate_hypotheses.hypothesis: The checkout API deployment (dep-1842) caused a code change leading to increased database latency which in turn caused higher error rates.
supporting_evidence: Checkout API completed the deployment at 10:01 UTC and checkout errors started increasing shortly after
Increased database latency occurred around the same time
contradicting_evidence: Checkout errors had been reported before the deployment as well
The previous incident with a similar symptom involved an expired service credential, not necessarily code changes.
evidence_needed: Earlier logs from checkout API for any pre-existing issues
Rollback of dep-1842 and observing if error rates decrease
Verification of database query plans and execution times before and after the deployment

candidate_hypotheses.hypothesis: The external payment provider outage caused increased failures in the checkout process.
supporting_evidence: The payment provider reported intermittent errors at around 10:04 UTC
Checkout errors also began increasing around this time.
contradicting_evidence: Database latency increased before the payment provider error reports were available
evidence_needed: Provider response codes and detailed logs of the payment failures
Impact on other services that are not related to checkout but depend on the same payment provider.

candidate_hypotheses.hypothesis: An expired service credential caused authentication issues, leading to increased checkout errors.
supporting_evidence: A previous similar incident involved an expired service credential
contradicting_evidence: No immediate evidence of any credentials expiring around the time of deployment.
evidence_needed: Review of all service credentials and their expiration dates before and during the deployment
Logs from authentication services related to checkout API

reversible_next_actions.action: Rollback dep-1842 and monitor for improvements in error rates.
conditions: If the rollback shows a decrease in error rates, it supports that the deployment may have caused the issue.

reversible_next_actions.action: Perform an analysis of database queries to identify any performance issues introduced by dep-1842.
conditions: If issues are found in query execution plans or code changes related to the API, this supports the hypothesis that the deployment caused the issue.

reversible_next_actions.action: Contact the external payment provider for more detailed logs and status updates about their service.
conditions: If they confirm that the outage was indeed a contributing factor, it supports that the checkout errors are due to external issues.

uncertainty_statement: The root cause of the increased checkout error rates is not yet confirmed. Timing alone does not establish causation. Further investigation into the deployment details, database performance metrics, and payment provider logs is necessary before a decision on rollback or other actions can be made with certainty.
